howItWorks.title: How does it work?
howItWorks.intro: You give a starting point and a distance, we build a real-world routable path down to the metre, preferring runner-friendly areas.
howItWorks.step1Body: Starting point (GPS or address), target distance (1 to 50 km), shape (loop or out-and-back), surface (road, trail, mixed) and discipline (running or cycling).
howItWorks.step2Body: We query OpenStreetMap (via Overpass) for parks, promenades, greenways, beaches and trails around you. Three POI are selected with bearing diversity in mind so a route doesn't stay stuck in a single neighbourhood.
howItWorks.step3Body: The open-source Brouter service computes the real-world trace using paths, sidewalks and tracks suited to your discipline. The distance is adjusted iteratively to land within ±5% of your target.
howItWorks.step4Body: Three variants are offered with different POI and bearings. Each shows actual distance, elevation gain, profile chart and can be exported to GPX or saved locally.
howItWorks.limitsBody: Quality depends on OpenStreetMap coverage in your area. In sparsely-mapped rural zones, the algorithm falls back to blind triangulation with water-point filtering. Swimming is not supported (no on-water routing).
howItWorks.privacyBody: Your starting position is sent to Brouter (routing), Nominatim (address search) and Overpass (POI) for the duration of the requests. No identifier is attached, nothing is stored server-side. You can disable the generator entirely in Settings.
howItWorks.sourcesBody: Data: © OpenStreetMap contributors. Routing: Brouter. Address search: Nominatim. POI: Overpass API.
